statement: Every triangle-free graph with maximum degree 4 is 3-colorable.
definitions: Simple graph; 'maximum degree 4' means Delta(G) <= 4 (a 4-regular witness satisfies either reading); proper vertex coloring with 3 colors.
ground_truth_witness: The Chvatal graph on vertices 0..11 with the 24 edges 0-1 0-4 0-6 0-9 1-2 1-5 1-7 2-3 2-6 2-8 3-4 3-7 3-9 4-5 4-8 5-10 5-11 6-10 6-11 7-8 7-11 8-10 9-10 9-11. It is 4-regular (so maximum degree 4) and triangle-free (girth 4), yet exhaustive search shows it admits no proper 3-coloring; its chromatic number is 4.
reference_authority: online-cited counterexample (MO/MSE/CS.SE/Wikipedia) with verify script, verified per partB_feasibility records

skeptic.objection: Reference verified: the listed 24-edge graph is 4-regular, triangle-free, not 3-colorable, 4-colorable (exhaustive). Claim precise under either reading of 'maximum degree 4'. Genuinely harder than the roster's triangle-free items: the Grötzsch graph (roster witness for cb-mse-r03/cb-gt09) has Delta=5 and does NOT refute this claim, and Brooks gives chi<=4 so the solver must find a triangle-free 4-chromatic graph with Delta<=4 (Chvátal graph is the smallest 4-regular one). Distinct claim, distinct witness.
